name: Pocket Punch-Kick Cluster
notes: Throw a short, compact punch combination in the pocket, then an immediate low or body kick. Recoil the kicking leg and restore stance and guard. Stop if kick recoil, stance recovery, or guard slows.
equipment_note: Set the bag so punches and kicks land without reaching or chasing.

name: Cover-Hook-Kick Burst
notes: Partner gives one controlled short attack. Cover, answer with a compact hook and low or body kick, recoil the kick, then restore stance and guard. Fully reset; do not trade freely. Stop if stance recovery slows.
equipment_note: Partner controls the feed and holds Thai pads at close range.

name: Check-Return Pocket Burst
notes: Partner feeds a controlled low kick during a close exchange. Check, return aggressively inside the pocket with a compact punch-kick answer, recoil the kick, and restore stance and guard.
equipment_note: Partner gives a safe low-kick feed and presents Thai pads for the immediate pocket answer.

name: Pocket Knee Reentry Burst
notes: Complete a short exchange, use a brief frame and separation, then take a valid Thai-pad knee opening and add one compact punch. Restore stance and guard immediately; release immediately after the knee. Stop if posture or stance recovery slows.
equipment_note: Partner holds Thai pads, controls the knee entry, and avoids live impact.

name: Punch-Kick Exchange Intervals
notes: Repeat separate 2-4 strike pocket exchanges using punches and a low or body kick. Recoil every kick, restore stance and guard, then begin the next exchange. No endless flurries; keep compact mechanics under fatigue.
equipment_note: Work at pocket range on a secured heavy bag without chasing its swing.

name: Guard-and-Low-Kick Answer
notes: Partner varies controlled short punch attacks. Cover, catch, or roll as appropriate; answer with a short punch and low kick, recoil the kick, then restore stance and guard before the next cue. Win each exchange, then restore position.
equipment_note: Partner controls contact and presents Thai pads for each close-range answer.

name: Pocket Body-Head-Leg Intervals
notes: The holder varies body, head, and leg target availability. Build compact 2-4 strike punch-kick exchanges, recoil each kick, and restore stance and guard between exchanges. Read the open target rather than repeating a fixed combination.
equipment_note: Partner uses Thai pads to present safe, changing close-range targets.

name: Close-Range Exchange Rounds
notes: Work partner-led short pocket exchanges at a sustainable pace. Mix compact punches with low or body kicks, recoil every kick, and restore stance, guard, and posture before a brief reset or re-engagement. Do not chase between exchanges.
equipment_note: Partner controls the pace and uses Thai pads for safe mixed-strike exchanges.

name: Inside Decision Rounds — Kickboxing / Muay Thai
notes: Partner unpredictably presents a short punch attack, low- or body-kick cue, brief close-range entry, or cover opening. Read the exchange; cover, check, catch, or parry as appropriate; answer compactly with punches or a kick, then recoil and restore stance and guard before resetting or re-engaging. Use a controlled Thai-pad knee only on a valid close-range opening.
equipment_note: Partner controls all feeds and holds Thai pads; knees are controlled with no live impact.

name: MMA Pocket Power Cluster
notes: Exchange at close range, then deliver a compact 2–4 strike burst. Restore stance with hips underneath, balanced posture and hands ready for an appropriate takedown defence. Stop if the athlete becomes square, reaches, or cannot remain shot-ready.
equipment_note: The partner holds Thai pads and stays close enough for clean strikes without chasing.

name: Exchange-Sprawl-Return Burst
modality: close exchange with live takedown decision
notes: Begin a short striking exchange. The partner may make a genuine committed shot. Read the attack, use appropriate takedown defence only when needed, create safe separation, return 1–2 compact strikes, and restore stance and base.
equipment_note: Use Thai pads for the return. Agree controlled shot intensity and a safe mat area.

name: Clinch-Break Strike Burst
modality: brief clinch interruption and strike on break
notes: The partner establishes one controlled brief tie-up. Frame and create safe separation, fire a compact 2–3 strike combination on the break, then restore stance and base. Reset if the tie-up becomes prolonged hand fighting.
equipment_note: Use Thai pads after a light, agreed tie-up. No live elbows.

name: Ground-and-Pound Position Burst
notes: Start from an already-secured mount, half-guard top, or stable postured guard-top position. Maintain base and posture through a compact 3–5 second punch or padded-strike burst. Regain stable posture and base, then fully reset. Stop when output compromises position.
equipment_note: Use a grappler dummy or fixed pad target. Do not chase position or use uncontrolled elbows or hammerfists.

name: Pocket Strike-Shot Intervals
modality: repeated close exchanges with live shot decisions
notes: The partner unpredictably presents a short striking exchange, a genuine committed shot, or no shot. Exchange compactly, defend only when necessary, make a brief strike return or safe separation, and restore stance and base before the next exchange.
equipment_note: Use controlled shots and Thai pads. The athlete must read the partner rather than pre-sprawl.

name: Frame-Break-Reengage Intervals
modality: close striking with brief tie-up interruptions
notes: Work through repeated short-range striking exchanges. The partner occasionally adds a brief tie-up. Frame for safe separation, score with a short immediate strike sequence, restore stance and base, then read the next exchange. Stop and redesign if hand fighting occupies most of the interval.
equipment_note: Keep each tie-up brief and controlled. Use Thai pads for clean strike targets.

name: Cage Pocket Exchange Intervals
modality: balanced close exchanges near the cage
notes: Start near the cage, not fixed against it. The partner gives short striking exchanges, occasional shot or brief tie-up threats, and lateral movement. Strike compactly, stay balanced, use appropriate defence, then angle or reset when position collapses and restore stance and base. The goal is scoring safely, not driving the partner backwards.
equipment_note: A padded wall may replace the cage. Use controlled glove or pad contact.

name: MMA Close-Exchange Flow
notes: At a sustainable pace, the partner mixes short striking exchanges, genuine level-change threats, brief tie-ups, separation and disengagement. Read each threat, use appropriate defence, continue scoring or disengage, and restore stance and base. Decision quality must stay clear.
equipment_note: Use Thai pads and controlled contact. Reduce pace before reading or stance quality falls.

name: MMA Brawler Decision Rounds
notes: The partner unpredictably presents a short striking exchange, level change, genuine committed shot, brief tie-up, or disengagement. Choose whether to continue the exchange, defend, frame, create safe separation, strike on the break, reset, or re-engage. Restore stance and base after each action; responses are not pre-called.
equipment_note: Use Thai pads and controlled MMA feeds. Keep the pace low enough for accurate decisions.

name: Clinch Hold & Knee Complex
notes: Builds plumb-position endurance while striking. Alternate between single collar and double collar ties. (90% effort)

name: MMA Clinch Position Flow
notes: Connect at low intensity against light live resistance. Pummel for useful underhook or overhook position, establish head position and posture, then stabilise. As the partner changes position, recover useful standing connection without completing a takedown.
equipment_note: Partner gives light positional resistance. Use controlled contact and no neck cranks.

name: Cage Position Flow
modality: sustainable favourable and unfavourable cage positioning
notes: Flow between being pinned to the cage and holding favourable cage control. Against light live resistance, gain inside and head position, answer underhook battles, turn attempts, escapes and brief separation, then reverse or re-establish useful standing connection.
equipment_note: Use a partner and padded cage or padded wall simulation. No uncontrolled impact into the surface.

name: Reactive MMA Clinch Rounds
notes: The partner unpredictably pummels, frames, changes level, turns, separates, pressures towards the cage, circles away or shows a short-strike opening. Choose to pummel, frame, gain an underhook and head position, stuff the level change, turn, separate, make one controlled pad strike or reconnect. Keep decisions sustainable and recover standing control; responses are not pre-called.
equipment_note: Partner gives sustainable live resistance and holds a Thai pad for controlled strikes. No live knees or elbows to the head.

name: Underhook Position Burst
notes: From standing connection, explosively win a useful underhook and head position against controlled resistance, stabilise posture and balance, then reset. Success is secure standing position, not takedown completion.
equipment_note: Partner provides controlled positional resistance. Release safely on the reset.

name: Cage Turn Burst
notes: Start in an unfavourable cage relationship. Establish useful inside and head position, turn the partner to reverse the position, gain favourable cage control and stabilise before resetting. Do not slam or throw.
equipment_note: Use a partner and padded cage or padded wall simulation. Keep the turn controlled with no uncontrolled wall impact.

name: Level-Change Stuff-and-Recover Burst
modality: standing clinch recovery after a level-change threat
notes: From standing connection, recognise the partner’s controlled level-change or takedown-entry cue, stuff the entry, regain useful head and inside position, stabilise the clinch, then reset. Success means standing clinch control is recovered; do not sprawl for conditioning or finish a takedown.
equipment_note: Partner gives a controlled entry cue on a safe surface. Keep the exchange standing and reset once position is stable.

name: Cage Position Intervals
notes: Battle repeatedly for the pin, underhook and head position as the partner contests turns, reversals, escapes and re-pins. Preserve posture, balance, inside position and decision quality. Reduce resistance if the work becomes sloppy wrestling.
equipment_note: Use live partner resistance at a padded cage or padded wall simulation. No uncontrolled impact into the surface.

name: Clinch Strike-Control Intervals
modality: short strikes conditional on standing clinch control
notes: Win or maintain useful standing clinch position, take one short controlled punch or knee opportunity on the pad, and immediately recover head and arm position as the partner contests. Reposition, keep awareness of the MMA takedown threat, and strike again only when control allows. A strike that collapses connection is a poor rep.
equipment_note: Partner gives live positional resistance and presents a Thai pad. Use controlled pad contact; no live knees or elbows to the head.

name: Pummel-to-Attack Intervals
notes: Pummel against active resistance and first win useful underhook, head or cage position. Then choose one suitable action: one short controlled pad strike, a cage turn, or a controlled takedown-entry position. Reset and re-engage. Do not complete a takedown or continue into a wrestling chain.
equipment_note: Partner actively contests position and presents a Thai pad when appropriate. Keep strikes and entry positions controlled.

name: MMA Clinch Decision Rounds
modality: high-density MMA clinch decisions under fatigue
notes: Under higher live resistance, the partner unpredictably creates an underhook battle, cage pin or reversal, frame, level change, separation, short-strike opening, circle-away or takedown-entry opportunity. Choose to pummel, frame, gain head and inside position, defend the level change, turn, separate, make one controlled pad strike, establish an entry position or reconnect. Preserve decisions under fatigue and recover standing control; do not finish takedowns.
equipment_note: Use a partner, Thai pad and padded cage or padded wall simulation. Control all contact and wall pressure; no live knees or elbows to the head.

name: Clinch Position Flow
notes: From connection, gain useful inside arm and head position, keep posture, then recover and stabilise as the partner changes grips, angle and position with light resistance. No maximal pulling.
equipment_note: Partner provides light, changing resistance in a Thai clinch position.

name: Posture-Control Knee Flow
notes: Establish useful clinch control against light resistance, create one valid opening, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, restore stance and posture, then regain position before scoring again.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Reactive Clinch Position Rounds
notes: Partner unpredictably changes grips, frames, straightens, turns, separates or presents a knee opening. Choose to pummel, frame, re-posture, turn, reconnect, score one controlled knee or stabilise; no pre-called response.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Posture-Break Knee Burst
notes: From connection, win safe posture control against resistance, briefly disrupt balance, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, then immediately regain a stable clinch position.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Turn-and-Knee Burst
notes: Establish useful clinch position against resistance, turn and off-balance without throwing, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, then restore position.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Frame-Reconnect Burst
notes: Partner frames or creates brief separation. Maintain balance, work around the frame, reconnect, regain useful inside position and stabilise. Do not add a striking flurry.
equipment_note: Partner provides positional resistance through a realistic frame or brief separation from Thai clinch.

name: Clinch Reposition Intervals
notes: Partner contests inside position, posture, angle, turns and head or arm control. Repeatedly gain, lose or change, recover and stabilise. Reduce resistance before movement becomes wrestling.
equipment_note: Partner provides active Thai clinch resistance and reduces it if technique drifts towards wrestling.

name: Knee-and-Recover Intervals
notes: Gain useful clinch against resistance, land one controlled knee to Thai pads, recover posture and feet, solve the partner’s renewed position contest, then regain control before scoring again.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Grip-Fight-to-Score Intervals
notes: Partner actively contests arm and inside position. Hand-fight to useful control, create a valid opening, score one controlled knee to Thai pads, then reset and solve the next contest. No free knee.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Clinch Decision Rounds
notes: Partner increases positional resistance and feeds frames, turns, posture battles, knee threats and brief separations at a high but controlled rate. Maintain decision quality: pummel, frame, re-posture, turn, off-balance, reconnect or score one controlled knee to Thai pads, then restore useful position before solving the next problem.
equipment_note: Partner gives realistic positional resistance; use Thai pads as listed for controlled knees.

name: Inside Position Flow
notes: Use light continuous partner resistance. Gain inside hand or forearm position, keep the feet underneath the body and maintain posture as the partner changes arm position. Regain useful connection, then separate under control and restore stance and guard. No takedowns, neck cranking, or extended collar ties.
equipment_note: The partner changes arm position at a sustainable pace and reduces resistance if posture or balance deteriorates.

name: Frame-Separate-Reset Flow
notes: From light partner connection, establish an appropriate forearm frame, create legal space, separate cleanly, and restore guard and boxing stance immediately. Reset only after balance and readiness return. Do not push the partner across the ring or hold statically.
equipment_note: The partner supplies light inward pressure and allows a clean technical separation.

name: Tie-Up Position Burst
notes: Begin at first contact. Explosively gain useful inside arm position against controlled resistance, stabilise posture and balance briefly, then release and reset in stance. Stop the rep if it becomes a body lock, throw, or wrestling exchange.
equipment_note: The partner gives controlled arm-position resistance without changing levels or attempting a takedown.

name: Turn-and-Separate Burst
notes: Control the connection, use foot position and upper-body contact to turn or reposition the partner, then separate cleanly and restore stance and guard in the better boxing position. No throws, trips, or prolonged body locks.
equipment_note: The partner gives controlled positional resistance and stays balanced throughout the turn.

name: Smother-Return Burst
notes: The holder gives one controlled short punching action. Smother its punching space, establish brief arm or forearm control, separate into legal punching space, land one or two short punches to the mitts, then reset stance and guard. Stop if control is skipped or live head contact develops.
equipment_note: The partner wears mitts, keeps the opening action controlled, and presents targets only after legal space appears.

name: Inside Position Intervals
notes: Contest inside hand position, forearm control, posture and balance repeatedly. Keep the feet underneath the body, the head stable and guard responsibility intact while regaining useful connection. Separate cleanly and restore guard at the end of each interval. Reduce resistance if either boxer starts wrestling or holding statically.
equipment_note: The partner varies arm position and gives moderate continuous resistance without takedown attempts.

name: Control-Separate-Punch Intervals
notes: Repeatedly establish brief arm or forearm control, separate into legal punching room, land one to three short punches to the mitts, then reconnect or reset in stance. The control problem must come before every return. Reduce output if the drill becomes static holding or free pocket trading.
equipment_note: The partner contests the connection moderately, then presents mitt targets only after clean separation.

name: Reactive Clinch Decision Rounds
notes: The partner unpredictably ties one arm, squares chest-to-chest, presses inward, begins separating, exposes brief punching space, or smothers offence. Without a pre-called response, choose to frame, regain inside position, turn, smother, separate, or punch the mitts when legal space appears. Restore stance and guard after each exchange and lower resistance if decisions or balance deteriorate.
equipment_note: The partner wears mitts and varies realistic close-contact problems at a sustainable pace; punches land only on the mitts.

name: Max Knee & Sprawl Complex
notes: Builds output for finishing exchanges against the ropes/cage. Alternate between straight and diagonal knees. (95% effort)

name: Dutch Clinch Drill
duration: 30s clinch knees → 30s short punches → x5 rounds
notes: Develops Dutch-style combination striking from the clinch. (90% effort)
equipment_note: Thai pads or heavy bag ideal

name: Band-Resisted Whizzer & Sprawl Complex
notes: Develops late-round takedown defense from overhook positions. (90% effort)

name: Read & Counter Flow
notes: Partner gives controlled jab, rear straight, hook or forward-entry cues. Defend or intercept, return a light counter, then regain stance and range. Keep the pace easy; reduce cue variety if the athlete guesses or loses shape.

name: Counter Shadow Flow
notes: Cycle through named imagined cues: jab, rear straight, hook and forward entry. Use the matching defence, counter at light speed, then angle out and reset. Do not free-punch between cues.

name: Defensive Position Flow
notes: Use a fixed cue sequence: jab to slip, straight to parry, hook to roll. Add one light counter after each defence, then recover stance and range before the next cue.

name: Slip-Cross Burst
notes: Holder shows a jab cue. Slip outside, fire one immediate cross counter, then step to safe range and reset. Stop the set if timing slows, defence gets loose or stance recovery deteriorates.

name: Pull-Straight Burst
notes: Holder steps in with a straight-punch cue. Pull just out of range, return one straight immediately, then recover stance and distance. Every rep starts from the entry cue.

name: Check-Hook Pivot Burst
notes: Holder applies a controlled forward-pressure cue. Land a check-hook counter, pivot off the line, then reset at safe range. Reduce speed if the athlete crosses their feet or loses defensive shape.

name: Intercepting Straight Burst
notes: Holder makes a clear forward-entry cue. Land an immediate straight stop-hit, exit off line, and reset. Use one full-quality response only; do not turn it into a combination sprint.

name: Reactive Counter Choice
notes: Holder gives one unpredictable jab, rear straight, hook or forward-entry cue. Select the correct defence or intercept, counter immediately, then reposition. Reduce cue choices if the athlete starts guessing.

name: Parry-Return Intervals
notes: Holder feeds repeated straight-punch cues at a controlled pace. Parry, return a straight immediately, then regain guard and range before the next feed. Accuracy and clean defence come before volume.

name: Defend-Counter-Exit Intervals
notes: Partner gives controlled single attacks. Defend, counter with one to three punches, angle out, and reset before the next cue. The athlete cannot initiate freely.

name: Random Attack Counter Rounds
notes: Holder attacks unpredictably with jab, rear straight, hook or forward entry. Read, defend or intercept, counter, then reposition. Slow the feeds if timing or stance recovery declines.

name: Counter Quality Rounds
notes: Holder repeats varied attack cues under a steady pace. Athlete defends or intercepts, counters accurately, then resets. Keep timing, accuracy and defensive shape intact; never chase uncontrolled punch volume.

name: Counter Kick Matrix
notes: Partner gives controlled low- and body-kick cues. Read the kick, check, make an immediate light return kick, recoil it, then recover stance and guard before the next feed. Alternate sides without chasing pace; balance and clean position end every repetition.
equipment_note: Partner feeds one controlled kick only after stance and guard are restored.

name: Teep Intercept Flow
notes: Partner gives a clear forward-entry cue. Read the step, intercept with a light teep, recoil the kicking leg, replace the foot, recover stance, guard and range, then accept the next feed.
equipment_note: Partner presents a body pad and varies the timing of controlled forward entries.

name: Kick Defence Reset Flow
notes: Partner mixes controlled low-kick and body-kick cues. Read each feed, check, forearm-parry or step just outside range as appropriate, make one light kick return, recoil, then recover stance and defensive position. Do not preselect the defence.
equipment_note: Partner limits the menu to safe, controlled kicks and allows a full reset.

name: Check-Return Kick Burst
notes: Partner gives one low-kick cue. Read and check it, fire one explosive immediate return kick, recoil quickly, and recover stance and guard inside the effort. Stop if timing, balance, recoil or defensive shape drops.
equipment_note: Partner gives one safe low-kick feed per effort and holds for the return.

name: Pull-Kick Counter Burst
notes: Partner cues a jab or rear straight. Read it, pull or slide just beyond the strike, make one immediate body- or low-kick return, recoil, then recover stance, guard and range. One clean response per effort; stop if the athlete guesses.
equipment_note: Partner wears Thai pads and feeds one controlled straight punch per effort.

name: Intercept & Counter Mitts
notes: Holder gives either a forward-entry cue or a long straight cue. Read the action: teep the entry, or parry the straight and return a straight punch or kick. Make one explosive response, then recoil and recover stance, guard and range. The holder chooses the cue, not the athlete.
equipment_note: Partner uses Thai pads for the controlled straight cue and the safe teep or counter target.

name: Reactive Counter Choice — Kickboxing
notes: Partner unpredictably chooses jab, rear straight, low kick or forward entry. Perceive the attack, select a suitable defence or interception, make one immediate punch, kick or teep counter, then recoil and recover stance and defensive position. Do not reveal the answer before the cue; stop if guessing begins.
equipment_note: Partner uses controlled contact and Thai pads for the selected return.

name: Check-Return Intervals — Kickboxing
notes: Partner varies the timing and side of controlled low- and body-kick feeds. Read, check, make an immediate kick return, recoil, and recover stance and guard before every new cue. Reduce feed rate if balance, timing or defensive shape fades.
equipment_note: Partner holds Thai pads and waits for a complete stance reset between feeds.

name: Defend-Counter-Reposition Intervals — Kickboxing
notes: Partner mixes straight-punch, low-kick, body-kick and forward-entry cues. Read and defend, evade or intercept, make a short immediate counter of no more than two strikes, then move laterally and recover stance, guard and range. The next feed waits for the reset.
equipment_note: Partner uses controlled feeds and presents pads for realistic returns.

name: Random Attack Counter Rounds — Kickboxing
notes: Partner unpredictably feeds a jab, rear straight, low kick, body kick or forward entry. Athlete cannot initiate: read the attack, choose a sound defence or interception, counter immediately, recoil kicks, then recover stance and defensive position with a lateral reset. Lower the feed rate when choices or shape deteriorate.
equipment_note: Partner controls contact and feed density while presenting safe pad targets.

name: Counter Knee Matrix
notes: Partner cues a controlled forward punch or close-range entry. Read it, cover or frame to stop the entry, make an immediate knee counter, recoil and place the leg back in stance, then recover stance, frame, guard and position before the next feed. This is an entry counter, not a prolonged clinch exchange.
equipment_note: Partner wears Thai pads and gives controlled entries without extended clinch fighting.

name: MMA Read & Counter Flow
notes: Partner unpredictably feeds a controlled jab, rear straight, kick, forward entry or level-change cue. Athlete reads the threat, uses a suitable defence or interception, makes one light counter to the pads, then restores stance and range before the next feed. Keep the pace easy and reduce cue variety if the athlete starts guessing.

name: Strike-Shot Transition Flow
notes: Partner alternates unpredictably between a controlled striking attack and a level-change or shot cue. Athlete reads which threat is present, uses striking defence or appropriate hip and takedown defence, makes one light counter to the pads after safe separation, then recovers stance and range. Keep shot feeds submaximal; this is not a repeated-sprawl circuit.

name: Cage Counter Movement Flow
notes: Partner applies controlled forward pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete reads the pressure, defends or frames, angles away, makes one light counter to the pads, regains open space, then resets in stance. Position restored is the success condition; lower pressure if footwork or defensive shape breaks down.
equipment_note: Use a wall as the practical cage substitute; partner controls pressure and presents safe pad targets.

name: Sprawl-Counter Burst
notes: Partner gives one clear, committed but controlled shot cue. Athlete reads it, sprawls or uses appropriate hip defence, creates safe striking separation, lands one immediate counter to the pad, then resets completely. Stop the set when reaction speed, hip position or stance recovery declines.

name: Intercepting Knee Entry Burst
notes: Partner controls a committed forward or level-change cue and presents a Thai-pad target. Where technically appropriate, athlete reads the entry, intercepts the pad with one knee, recoils, then restores stance and defensive position. Never use uncontrolled live knee contact; stop if timing, balance or recoil deteriorates.

name: Level-Change Uppercut Burst
notes: Holder gives a controlled level-change cue and presents a mitt target. Athlete reads the cue, uses the uppercut as a specific interception option, fires once to the mitt, exits off line, then recovers stance and guard. This is not a universal takedown response; stop if the athlete guesses or loses defensive shape.

name: Stuff-Shot Counter Exit
notes: Partner gives one controlled takedown-entry cue. Athlete reads and stuffs or otherwise defends the entry, establishes safe separation, lands one short counter to the pad, exits laterally into open space, then resets completely. End the effort if it becomes prolonged wrestling or stance recovery slows.

name: Reactive MMA Counter Choice
notes: Partner gives one unpredictable cue from a restricted set: jab, rear straight, kick, forward pressure, level change or controlled takedown entry. Athlete reads the threat, chooses a sound defence or interception, counters immediately to the pads, then repositions and recovers stance. Reduce the cue set if guessing begins and stop when reaction quality falls.

name: Strike-or-Shot Counter Intervals
notes: Partner repeatedly alternates unpredictably between controlled strike and takedown-entry cues. Athlete reads each threat, uses the appropriate defence, counters briefly to the pads, recovers guard and stance, then waits for the next cue without free initiation. Lower feed density if defensive shape or decision accuracy breaks down.

name: Cage Defend-Counter-Escape
notes: Partner applies controlled pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete reads the pressure, frames, uses an underhook or angle where appropriate, creates safe separation, lands one short counter to the pads, then exits into open space and restores stance. Avoid static clinch grinding; reduce pressure when posture or escape footwork fails.
equipment_note: Use a wall as the practical cage substitute; partner controls pressure and pad contact.

name: Failed Shot Punish & Reset
notes: Partner gives a controlled failed or defended takedown entry and presents pad targets. Athlete reads the failed entry, establishes safe position, delivers a one-to-three-strike counter, disengages, then restores stance and range before the next cue. Do not extend the exchange into grappling; lower feed density if defensive position fades.

name: MMA Counter Decision Rounds
notes: Partner unpredictably provides controlled strikes, kicks, level changes, takedown entries or pressure toward a wall or cage. Athlete cannot freely initiate: read, defend or intercept, counter briefly to the pads, recover stance or open space, then wait for the next problem. Lower cue density when choices, mechanics or defensive recovery deteriorate.
equipment_note: Use a wall as the practical cage substitute and pads for all hard counter targets.

name: Ring Perimeter Flow
notes: Circle in stance at a relaxed pace. Every 8-12 seconds, jab or feint, make an angle exit, then restore preferred range.

name: Ring Escape Flow
notes: Partner gives forward or lateral pressure cues. Move, pivot or L-step, regain open space, then reset stance and range.

name: Jab Volume & Position
notes: Maintain frequent jab output. Every jab or double jab must finish with balanced stance, defensive recovery and preferred range restored.

name: Entry-Score-Exit Bursts
notes: Explosive step-in, land 1-3 straight shots, then exit immediately at an angle. Full-quality reset before the next rep.

name: Long-Range Movement Flow
notes: Move at long range behind the jab and long guard. Keep the stance narrow enough to kick, then exit laterally; lower the pace if balance changes.

name: Backstep Counter Reset
notes: On the advance cue, make a controlled backstep, fire a straight counter, then exit laterally and restore range.

name: Straight-Shot Re-Angle
notes: Fire one explosive jab-cross or rear straight, retract cleanly, then make a 30-45 degree angle exit before resetting.

name: Open-Space Movement Flow
notes: Move economically in MMA stance. Enter to score, then leave before an imagined wrestling connection. Keep the centre and do not drift towards the marked boundary on consecutive exchanges.

name: Cage-Aware Range Flow
notes: Use a marked boundary. Manage the partner and boundary together. Reposition laterally rather than retreating straight on consecutive exchanges, and regain open space before starting again.

name: Level-Change Respect Flow
notes: The partner mixes normal movement with genuine level changes. Maintain range, angle off or move the hips back as needed. Only sprawl when the partner can reach the legs, then restore stance and preferred range.

name: Intercept-and-Exit Burst
notes: The partner enters aggressively from shot range. Intercept with one appropriate long strike and angle out before body contact. Stop the set if reaction speed, stance or defensive shape drops.

name: Strike-Sprawl-Reset Burst
notes: Score once. The partner may strike, level-change or stay out. Only sprawl when a genuine shot reaches the legs; otherwise use range, angle or hip-back readiness. Reset stance and range. Stop if the cue is read late.

name: Entry-Score-Angle Burst
notes: Enter for one clean score and immediately take an angle before the partner can establish wrestling contact. Recover stance at safe range. Stop if the exit becomes upright or square.

name: Fence-Escape Burst
notes: Begin one step from a marked boundary, not pinned to it. As the partner closes, use a strike, frame or angle and regain open space laterally. Reset if body contact becomes established. Stop when stance or defensive shape drops.

name: Reactive Range Decision Burst
notes: The partner gives one unpredictable cue: striking advance, genuine level change or no entry. Select an intercept and exit, shot defence, or patient range hold. Do not force an action. Stop if response speed or stance drops.

name: Cage Escape Intervals
notes: Use a marked boundary. The partner repeatedly advances from open range. Escape laterally with movement, a strike or frame, then regain open space before the next exchange. Never retreat straight on consecutive exchanges. Reduce output if cage awareness drops.

name: Strike-Level-Change Decision Rounds
notes: The partner mixes striking advances, genuine level changes and feints. Identify the threat before choosing range, angle, hip-back defence or a sprawl. Reset at preferred range. Reduce output if recognition becomes late.

name: In-Out MMA Striking Rounds
notes: Enter for short scoring exchanges, exit before wrestling contact and recover stance at long range. The partner may threaten a shot during either transition. Reduce output if the athlete stays extended or loses hip-back readiness.

name: Anti-Fence Range Rounds
notes: Use a marked boundary. Score while protecting open-space position. Circle before the boundary blocks the exit and refuse prolonged backward drift. Reduce output if stance, level-change awareness or boundary checks deteriorate.

name: Failed-Entry Reset Intervals
notes: The partner sometimes removes the target or blocks the entry. After a miss, rebuild stance, protect the hips and exit before body contact. Do not chase the failed score. Reduce output if recovery needs more than one step.

name: Intercept-Reposition Rounds
notes: The partner repeatedly enters from striking or shot range. Intercept when safe, take an angle and recover open space before the next entry. Do not admire the score. Reduce output if exits become straight or late.

name: Long-Range MMA Decision Rounds
notes: Use a marked boundary. The partner mixes passive movement, striking pressure, level changes and boundary cuts. Choose long strikes, patient range holds, angles or shot defence without automatic sprawls. Reduce output if decisions become guessed or cage awareness fades.

name: Range Recovery Under Pressure
notes: The partner briefly crowds from a safe live position. Use stance, frame, angle or a short intercept to leave before a wrestling connection settles. Regain open space before scoring again. Stop if posture, defence or level-change recognition breaks down.

name: Teep Range-Control Flow
notes: Use the teep only from a measured range. Recover the kicking leg into stance before moving, then circle as the bag returns. Reset if the bag movement pulls the stance out of shape.

name: Ring Generalship Rounds
notes: Score with 1-3 shots, then exit at an angle. Do not stay square and do not retreat straight back repeatedly.

name: Range Reset Intervals
notes: Partner advances intermittently. Use the jab, step-slide or backstep, then reset laterally to preferred range.

name: Long-Weapon Exit Flow
notes: The holder advances lightly. Score with a jab, teep or long kick, recover stance, and exit laterally rather than retreating straight back. Lower the pace if the exit becomes a straight retreat.

name: Flicker’s Endurance
notes: 1-2s only, reset stance after each combo. (Fast twitch focus)

name: Precision Under Pace
notes: Maintain straight-shot accuracy with movement between exchanges. Speed may reduce slightly, but stance, accuracy and defensive recovery must stay clean.

name: Punch-Slide Repeatability
notes: Inside each work minute, perform a 5-8 second fast straight-punch burst, immediately slide or pivot away, move under control, then repeat.

name: Range Movement Flow
notes: Move economically in stance at preferred range. Every 10-15 seconds, score lightly, reposition off the return line and recover stance. Keep the pace low; reduce output if balance or foot position breaks down.

name: Range Reset Flow
notes: The partner changes distance with controlled forward or lateral pressure. Restore preferred range with one short retreat and an angle when needed; do not retreat straight back on consecutive actions. Recover stance before the next cue.

name: Entry-Exit Burst
notes: From preferred range, enter explosively, make one clean scoring action, then exit to safe range and recover stance. Use maximal speed. Stop and reset if balance, speed or position deteriorates.

name: Range Intercept Burst
notes: The partner crosses preferred range without a fixed rhythm. Intercept only when the crossing action is clear, then leave the return line and restore range. Stop and reset if timing, stance or positional control deteriorates.

name: Lateral Escape Burst
notes: The partner advances from just outside scoring range. Make one short lateral or angled escape, recover stance and face the partner at usable range. Do not turn it into a long retreat. Stop and reset if speed, balance or position deteriorates.

name: Range Recovery Intervals
notes: Start from a compressed distance cue. Restore preferred range, score once, reposition, then repeat at a demanding pace. Do not retreat straight back on consecutive actions. Reduce output if stance or balance breaks down.

name: Score-Reposition Rounds
notes: Work in controlled exchanges at useful range. Every score must finish with angle or space gained and stance recovered before the next exchange. Reduce output if either athlete can no longer control distance or balance.

name: Movement Economy Rounds
notes: Maintain preferred range while adding a light score and reposition every 6-10 seconds. Use the fewest useful steps; no excessive bouncing, crossed feet or repeated straight retreat. Lower the pace if stance or distance control fades.

name: Reactive Distance Rounds
notes: The partner unpredictably enters, holds or gives ground. Choose whether to enter, hold range, intercept or exit, then recover stance and preferred range before the next cue. Reduce output if decisions become automatic or position breaks down.

name: Pressure Escape and Reset
notes: The partner applies controlled forward pressure. Escape with a short lateral or angled action, recover stance at usable range, score once, then reset. Do not rely on prolonged straight retreat. Reduce output if the escape no longer restores position.

name: Teep Range Reset
notes: From stance, teep into open space, retract cleanly, restore stance and regain long range before the next repetition.

name: Kick & Exit Flow
notes: Score with a low or body kick, recover the leg, then move off the return line and restore stance.

name: Switch-Side Rhythm
notes: Use controlled movement and kick efficiently from both sides. Keep the rhythm relaxed and finish every kick in stance.

name: Rear-Kick Power Singles
notes: Throw one maximum-quality rear body or low kick. Recoil fully and restore a balanced stance before resting.

name: Reactive Body-Kick Burst
notes: Partner moves and presents a target unpredictably. Recognise, position, kick explosively and recover stance. No target means no kick.

name: Low-Kick Exit Burst
notes: Land one hard low kick, recover the leg, restore stance and exit the opponent’s return line.

name: Check-Return Burst
notes: Read the kick cue, check, return immediately with a kick, then reset in stance.

name: Interception Kick Burst
notes: As the partner advances, intercept with a teep, side kick or back kick. Recover into a stance ready to defend another entry.

name: Dutch Target Call
notes: Throw jab-cross. The pad holder then presents a low or body target. Select the kick, recover stance and move.

name: Body-Kick Repeatability
notes: Move under control and take repeated body-kick opportunities. Reduce output if recoil slows or kicks consistently finish out of stance.

name: Switch-Kick Repeatability
notes: Repeat switch kicks from controlled movement. Reduce output if the switch rhythm, recoil or stance breaks down.

name: Low-High Decision Rounds
notes: Use the same initial presentation. Read the changing pad cue and choose the correct low, body or head target. Recover stance after every kick.

name: Kick-Punch Reposition
notes: Kick, recover stance, use straight punches as cover or a feint, then angle away instead of remaining stationary.

name: Long-to-Clinch Transition
notes: Use a teep or long kick. When the partner advances, recover stance and transition to a controlled knee or clinch position.

name: Kick Recoil Quality Rounds
notes: Repeat realistic kick opportunities. Stop the set if retraction slows or stance cannot be restored, then resume only when technique is sound.

name: Pressure-Kicker Rounds
notes: Maintain a credible kicking threat while the partner changes distance. Select the target, recoil and regain safe position after every attack.

name: Pressure Footwork Flow
notes: Stalk at a controlled pace while keeping stance width and head position. Do not cross the feet or chase straight behind an imagined opponent; reset stance after every entry.

name: Ring-Cut Flow
notes: Repeat left and right cutoff patterns at an easy technical pace. Step across the escape route before advancing; never cross the feet or become square.

name: Jab-to-Pressure Flow
notes: Use the jab to enter, take a useful forward position and reset stance after each entry. No clear target means no forced attack; circle out and rebuild.

name: Max-Power Bag Burst
notes: Deliver a five-second maximal-quality burst, then recover fully. Stop the burst if punch speed, shape or head position drops.

name: Explosive Cutoff Burst
notes: Close the escape route fast, score a short shadow combination and reset fully. Do not cross the feet or chase straight behind the opponent.

name: Entry-and-Score Burst
notes: Enter explosively, land two to four clean punches, then make a technical exit and regain stance. End the rep if the athlete becomes square.

name: Escape-Recatch Burst
notes: The partner escapes left or right; reposition immediately and re-establish pressure before scoring. Cut the route rather than following, then reset fully.

name: Corner Trap Burst
notes: Cut off the partner, hold a balanced trapping position and score two to four punches. Stop and reset if the feet cross or the stance becomes square.

name: Ring-Cutting Intervals
notes: The partner changes direction throughout. Cut the escape route before throwing and do not follow in a straight line; lower the pace if stance integrity is lost.

name: Pressure Combination Rounds
notes: Close distance behind a safe entry, combine in the pocket, then recover stance without giving up useful pressure. Reduce output if punch quality or defensive head position collapses.

name: Body-Head Pressure Intervals
notes: Alternate credible body and head combinations while keeping pressure between attacks. Regain stance before each new combination and reduce output if clean target changes disappear.

name: Cutoff-Reposition Intervals
notes: Apply pressure, read the partner’s escape, reposition and attack again. Cut the route before throwing; stop and reset if the athlete chases or crosses the feet.

name: Pocket Repeatability Rounds
notes: Repeat short-range combinations with brief stance resets inside each work bout. Reduce output if punch shape, head position or balance collapses.

name: Pressure Reset Intervals
notes: Shadow a safe entry and attack, recover stance, then rebuild pressure immediately. No opportunity means no forced attack; stop and reset if the feet become square.

name: Rope/Corner Pressure Rounds
notes: Keep the partner contained and score from a balanced stance rather than throwing nonstop. Maintain defensive head position; stop and reset whenever the athlete becomes square.

name: Pressure Decision Rounds
notes: The partner cues a left, right or backward escape. Select the correct cutoff, regain position, then score; no correct position means no forced attack.

name: Cage Cut & Re-Catch
notes: Guide the partner towards the fence at a controlled pace, deny the open-side exit and re-catch each direction change. Do not chase straight behind or cross the feet; reset stance before continuing.

name: Level-Threat Pressure Reset
notes: React to the partner’s level-change threat, protect stance and head position, then take back useful pressure before a short score. Stop the rep if the feet become square or balance is lost.

name: Punch-Clinch Reentry
notes: Score a short punch entry, connect to a safe clinch and settle balanced pressure. Regain stance before re-entering; stop if head position or clinch posture fails.

name: Strike-to-Fence Pressure
notes: Use a clean strike entry to move the partner towards the fence, connect position, then score again. Cut the lateral escape before attacking and reduce output if stance or defensive responsibility collapses.

name: Fence Escape Denial
notes: The partner attempts left and right fence escapes. Deny the route with feet and position before scoring; stop and reset if the athlete reaches, crosses feet or becomes square.

name: Kick-to-Pressure Flow
notes: Kick at a controlled pace, step down in stance and take useful forward position before the next attack. Do not fall square or force a follow-up when balance is poor.

name: Teep Walk-Down Reset
notes: Land a sharp teep, step forward under control and score a short follow-up before resetting. Stop the rep if the kicking leg drops out of stance or the athlete chases square.

name: Pressure-to-Clinch Transition
notes: Enter behind two or three clean strikes, connect to balanced clinch position and settle before release. Stop if head position, stance or posture is lost.

name: Kick-Step Pressure Rounds
notes: Link kicks to balanced step-down pressure and short punch combinations. Regain stance after every kick and reduce output if recoil, posture or target quality collapses.

name: Low-Kick Re-Catch Intervals
notes: Low kick, read the partner’s escape and cut the route before scoring again. Do not follow straight behind; stop and reset if kick recoil or stance recovery breaks down.

name: Takedown to Backtake Scramble
notes: Partner counters takedown — you must immediately transition to back control. (90% explosiveness)

name: Sprawl to Spin Drill
notes: Bands on hips to resist sprawl recovery. (Max speed)

name: Cage Wrestle Chaos
notes: Partner initiates cage clinch – you must reverse or escape. (Fight pace)

name: Turtle to Guard Scramble
notes: Partner starts in top turtle – you must recover guard or stand. (Explosive hips)

name: Shot to Granby Roll
notes: Emphasize smooth hip movement. (85% effort)

name: Stand-Up Sprint
notes: Bands around waist for resistance. (Max explosion)

name: Submission to Sweep Chain
notes: If sub fails, immediately chain to sweep. (Fast transitions)

name: Clinch to Takedown Scramble
notes: Partner resists – you must chain takedowns. (90% effort)

name: Guard Pass to Backtake
notes: If pass is blocked, transition to back. (Technical speed)

name: Strike to Takedown Scramble
notes: Coach signals shot after random strikes. (85% speed)

name: Arm Drag to Backtake
notes: Partner resists first 2 seconds. (Explosive pulls)

name: Front Headlock Escapes
notes: Partner starts in tight front headlock. (90% effort)

name: Cage to Center Scramble
notes: Partner pins to cage – you must escape to center. (Fight pace)

name: Rolling Backtake Drill
notes: Partner starts in turtle. (Fast transitions)

name: Strike to Submission Chain
duration: 3min rounds: combo → shot → sub attempt, 1min rest x 4
notes: Simulates fight-ending sequences. (85% effort)

name: Granby to Single Leg
notes: Partner provides light resistance. (Explosive)

name: Flying Sub Scramble
notes: Focus on landing in control. (Technical)

name: Clinch to Spin Drill
notes: Partner resists initial clinch. (Fast pivots)

name: Guard Recovery Sprint
notes: Partner starts in side control. (90% speed)

name: Standing Backtake Drill
notes: Partner defends first 3 seconds. (85% control)

name: Mat Shark
notes: Drill 3-step sub chains from guard. (85% effort)
equipment_note: Anchor bands to dummy for resistance

name: Stranglehold
notes: Partner resists first 5 sec, then taps. (90% squeeze)
equipment_note: Use gi lapel for no-gi grip variations

name: Limb Collector
notes: Bands on wrists to simulate opponent pulling back. (Explosive extensions)

name: Heel Hook Highway
notes: KB on ankle to simulate opponent weight. (Max control)

name: Guillotine Gauntlet
notes: Sandbag mimics sprawl pressure. (80% squeeze)

name: Twister Protocol
notes: Focus on grip transitions. (Slow, technical)

name: D’Arce Depth Charge
notes: Med ball simulates opponent’s head pressure. (Explosive shots)

name: Calf Slicer Pressure Drill
notes: KB on thigh to simulate opponent’s resistance. (Slow burn)

name: Kneebar Khaos
notes: Bands on ankles to simulate opponent retracting leg. (Explosive hips)

name: North-South Chokehold
notes: Sandbag on chest mimics opponent bridging. (85% effort)

name: Peruvian Necktie Drill
notes: Bands on dummy’s shoulders for resistance. (Fast setups)

name: Gogoplata Grinder
notes: Emphasize hamstring flexibility. (Slow, controlled)

name: Buggy Choke Crucible
notes: Partner starts in side control. (85% squeeze)

name: Electric Chair Sweep
notes: KB on hip to add resistance. (Explosive hips)

name: Bicep Slicer Drill
notes: Bands simulate opponent pulling arm free. (Slow burn)

name: Loop Choke Loop
notes: Partner resists initial grip. (80% speed)

name: Inverted Triangle Matrix
notes: Use wall to control inversion angle. (Technical)

name: Ezekiel Finishing Drill
notes: Focus on forearm pressure. (90% squeeze)

name: Anaconda Ambush
notes: Sandbag simulates sprawl weight. (Explosive entries)

name: Crucifix Collector
duration: 3min rounds: arm trap → choke, 1min rest x 4
notes: Partner tries to bench press escape. (85% control)

name: Toe Hold Torment
notes: Bands on foot for resistance. (Fast hands)

name: Mir Lock Madness
notes: KB on wrist to simulate opponent’s defense. (Slow grind)

name: Japanese Necktie Drill
notes: Focus on hip alignment. (Technical)

name: Pocket Power Cluster
notes: Throw 3-4 compact hooks or uppercuts in the pocket. Restore the high guard and stance immediately. Stop if punch mechanics, stance, or guard recovery deteriorate.
equipment_note: Set the bag so compact punches land without reaching.

name: Wall-Wrestler Pummel Rounds
notes: Pummel for underhooks while pressed against wall. Simulates cage work.

name: Teep Intercept Burst
notes: The holder advances unpredictably. Intercept only when the entry is genuinely there, recover stance, and take a short angle. Stop if recoil or balance slows.

name: Cover-Return Burst
notes: The holder gives one controlled short attack. Cover in a high guard, return 2-4 compact punches, then restore guard and stance. Fully reset; do not trade freely.
equipment_note: The holder controls contact and presents close-range targets.

name: Sprawl-to-Strike Intervals
notes: Sprawl, then spring up into 2 knees + 2 elbows.
equipment_note: Use wrestler mat for knee protection.

name: Submission Chain Fatigue Drill
notes: Cycle through 3 submission attempts without pausing.

name: Kick-and-Exit Burst
notes: Land one clean long kick, recover the kicking leg into stance, and exit laterally. Stop the set if speed or stance recovery deteriorates.

name: Sprawl-to-Takedown Reaction Drill
notes: Partner signals shot randomly. React with sprawl then immediate takedown.

name: Guillotine Shot Sprints
notes: Sprint 10m, drop to guillotine grip, reset. Repeat.

name: Switch-Kick Power Bursts
notes: Max-power roundhouse kicks with full hip rotation.

name: Takedown Shot Reaction Drill
notes: Partner points direction; shooter explodes that way.

name: Thai Plum Explosion Drill
notes: Yank partner's neck down with full power from plum position.

name: Sprawl-to-Shot Sprints
notes: Sprawl, then explode into double-leg shot. Full recovery between reps.
equipment_note: Use wrestler mat for knee protection.

name: Jab-Kick Entry Burst
notes: Enter behind a long jab, kick the called open target, regain stance, and leave on an angle. No target means no kick.

name: Body-Head Power Burst
notes: The holder presents the open body or head target. Switch levels with 2-4 compact hooks, uppercuts, or short straights, then regain guard and stance. Stop if mechanics deteriorate.
equipment_note: Hold the mitts at realistic close-range body and head positions.

name: Blast Double Sprints
notes: Sprint into explosive takedown finish.

name: Guillotine Shot Reactions
notes: Partner signals shot direction; shooter reacts with guillotine grip.

name: Rear-Kick Reposition Burst
notes: Score with the rear kick, recoil into stance, then reposition outside the return line. Reset fully if the bag swing pulls posture forward.

name: Reactive Sprawl Jumps
notes: Partner claps to signal sprawl. Max-height jump after.

name: Exchange-Reentry Burst
notes: Complete a short pocket exchange, take a half-step reset, then use the holder's opening to re-enter with a compact combination. Recover stance. Do not chase at long range.
equipment_note: The holder creates a brief separation and a realistic re-entry opening.

name: Takedown-to-Knee Drill
notes: Double-leg takedown into standing knee strike. Reset.

name: Reactive Long-Weapon Burst
notes: On the holder’s advance, choose jab, teep or long kick and angle away after scoring. Stop if the choice, recoil or exit loses speed.

name: BJJ Explosive Guard Pull
notes: Pull guard with immediate hip bump sweep attempt.

name: Dump Explosions
notes: Max-effort hip toss from clinch position.

name: Cage-Push Escapes
notes: Explosive push-off from pinned cage position.

name: Pocket Combination Intervals
notes: Repeat compact pocket combinations with a guard reset between each. Alternate body-head patterns. Reduce output if punches become arm-dominant, the stance widens, or the guard disappears.
equipment_note: Work close enough for compact hooks and uppercuts without leaning.

name: Teep Volume & Position
notes: Repeat measured teeps while holding preferred range and changing angle after each score. Reduce output if stance recovery or target selection breaks down.

name: Reshot Chains
notes: Initial shot > sprawl > immediate reshot. No pauses.

name: Kick-Exit Intervals
notes: Kick only from long range, recover stance, then exit laterally before resetting. Reduce output if recoil slows or feet cross.

name: Guard-and-Answer Intervals
notes: Respond to each controlled short-range attack with a cover, roll, or catch, then answer immediately and regain the high guard. Wait for the next cue; do not free-hit continuously. Reduce output if defence or stance deteriorates.
equipment_note: The holder varies controlled hooks, short straights, and body attacks.

name: Hip Slam Drill
notes: Max-power hip toss from double-collar tie.

name: Corner Knee Bursts
notes: Max-power knees to trapped bag. Full hip extension.
equipment_note: Angle bag to simulate opponent lean.

name: Scrambler's Standup Explosions
notes: From bottom position, explode to feet in one motion.

name: Pocket Exchange Rounds
notes: Use controlled short pocket exchanges with body-head variation, a high guard, and stable head position. Briefly reset between exchanges. Keep a sustainable pace and do not chase across the ring.
equipment_note: Partner contact stays controlled so technical quality is maintained.

name: Long Combination Rounds
notes: Build long combinations from jab or long guard and finish with an angled exit. Lower the pace if balance or clean target selection fades.

name: Long-Distance Shadowboxing
notes: Emphasize footwork and jab-cross out-fighting. (low-moderate)

name: Clinch Marching Rounds
notes: Maintain plum position while circling.

name: Grappler's Flow Roll
notes: No submissions - constant positional transitions.

name: Range-Recovery Intervals
notes: Check or long-guard the imagined attack, reset the feet, and restore kicking range without repeated straight-line retreat. Reduce output if stance widens.

name: Cage Cutting Footwork
notes: Practice cutting off octagon while shadowboxing.

name: Pummeling Endurance Rounds
notes: Hand-fighting only. No takedowns.

name: Brawler's Forward Shadow
notes: Aggressive forward movement with high guard.

name: Hybrid Stance Switch Drill
notes: Switch stances every 3 steps while navigating cones.

name: Octagon Footwork Gauntlet
notes: Touch all 8 cage sections in sequence.

name: Submission Hunter's Guard Retention
notes: Partner attempts passes while you maintain guard. (low-moderate)

name: Jab-Teep Control Rounds
notes: Use jab and teep to halt or redirect the holder’s advance. Recover stance before moving and reset if preferred range is lost.

name: Wrestler's Wall-Walk Drill
notes: From butt-scoot position, walk up wall to standing.

name: Pressure Fighter's Cutoff Circuit
notes: Mirror imaginary opponent while cutting off space.

name: Hybrid's Stance Transition Drill
notes: Switch between orthodox/southpaw every 5 steps. (low-moderate)

name: Clinch Fighter's Neck Endurance
notes: Maintain plum position against light resistance.

name: Scrambler's Turtle Recovery
notes: From turtle, stand up and circle out repeatedly.

name: Inside Decision Rounds
notes: Read unpredictable controlled short-range attacks, cover opportunities, or brief disengagements. Choose to cover, roll, catch, answer body or head, reset, or re-engage. Do not preselect the response; lower the pace if decisions or guard deteriorate.
equipment_note: The holder varies realistic close-range cues without calling a fixed response.

name: Kick-Reposition Rounds
notes: After every long kick, recoil into stance and reposition before scoring again. No stable stance means no next kick.

name: Kicker's Switch Stance March
notes: Switch stances every 10 steps with teep feints. (low-moderate)

name: Grappler's Standup Chain
notes: From bottom, stand up and immediately sprawl.

name: Pressure Fighter's Cutoff Shadow
notes: Advance while cutting off angles in mirror.

name: Clinch Fighter's Frame Endurance
notes: Maintain frames against partner's forward pressure.

name: Hybrid's Transition Circuit
notes: Alternate between striking and shot feints.

name: Scrambler's Hip Escape Marathon
notes: Continuous hip escapes down mat length.

name: Pressure-Escape Distance Rounds
notes: Use long guard, teep feints and lateral steps to escape pressure, then restore preferred range. Do not rely on repeated straight-line retreat.

name: Shadow Flow Rounds
notes: Emphasize footwork pivots and defensive slips between combos (60-70% effort)

name: Long-Range Decision Rounds
notes: Choose jab, teep or long kick from the holder’s cue, then recover stance and exit. Reduce output when decisions, recoil or range control lose quality.

name: Grappler's Blindfold Pummeling
notes: Forces reliance on grip/body feel over sight (30% effort)
